statement.p: Find the parabola of the form y=ax^2+b which best fits the points (-1,0), (5,5), (7,10) by minimizing the sum of squares, S, given by S=(a+b)^2+(25 a+b - 5)^2+(49 a+b- 10)^2.

static.solution:
a and b, so we set \frac{\partial S}{\partial a} = 2(a+b) + 50(25 a + b - 5) + 98(49 a + b - 10) = 0 and \frac{\partial S}{\partial b} = 2(a+b) + 2(25 a + b - 5) + 2(49 a + b - 10) = 0. Collecting terms, we get 6054 a + 150 b - 1230 = 0 and 150 a + 6 b - 30 = 0, and solving for a and b gives a = \frac{5}{24} and b = \frac{-5}{24}
Since there is only one critical point and S is unbounded as a,b\to\infty, this critical point is the global minimum. Therefore, the best fitting parabola is y=(\frac{5}{24})\, x^2 + (\frac{-5}{24}).
